🇬🇧 UK Daily Briefing | Thursday, 5 November 2026

1. 🛂 Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood makes statement on earned settlement
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has made a statement on earned settlement.

2. 📹 New laws will govern police use of facial recognition technology
The government is bringing in stronger laws to govern how police use facial recognition technology. The stated aim is to maximise public safety.

3. ⏰ Temporary Shortage List will expire on 31 December 2026
Employers can only assign certificates of sponsorship for occupations on the Temporary Shortage List before 31 December 2026. With about eight weeks left, the Home Office has said little about what happens next.

4. 💷 Interest rates expected to rise for first time in over three years
Most analysts are predicting rates will rise from 3.75% to 4%. It would be the first increase in more than three years.

5. 🛡️ UK is dangerously reliant on China for critical minerals, MPs find
A parliamentary investigation has found the UK is "dangerously" dependent on China for raw materials needed for the military, renewable energy infrastructure and AI. MPs on the business select committee urged a centralised policy.

6. 🚲 Ministers plan crackdown on e-bikes blocking pavements
A consultation led by the Department for Transport will consider parking standards, fleet sizes and insurance requirements. Ministers want to curb antisocial behaviour such as cyclists jumping red lights.

7. 🌊 Warming UK seas could reshape marine ecosystems, study warns
A four-year study warns that warming seas around the UK and wider north-east Atlantic could destabilise marine food webs, weaken ocean health and jeopardise food security by 2050.

8. 📈 Pound reaches highest level since Brexit referendum
The pound has reached its highest level against a basket of currencies since the Brexit referendum a decade ago.

Sources: GOV.UK Home Office, Free Movement, BBC, Guardian. Stories summarised from UK media reports. Images: Pixabay. Photos: Lauren Hurley / No 10 Downing Street / OGL 3, Wikimedia Commons.
